analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the last-updated date (line 3) and adds a head-side paragraph around lines 1960-1973. The paragraph says a JSON response_format (json_object or json_schema) on the Qwen template family now defaults to a closed (non-thinking) reasoning block unless the caller sets an explicit thinking control. It also says the coordinator prompt sidecar mirrors the rule so cache planning renders the same prompt, and that public prompt vectors pin it.

The two supplied units are base_text excerpts (lines 806-1611) of unchanged surrounding documentation. They do not contain the new paragraph, so I examined them as context only. They cover GLM5Next admission and memory ledger, prompt receipts, calibration, deadlines, and the prompt token cache.

No documentation edit changes a security control, and no code is supplied. I identified no regression, new attack surface or invalidated assumption against the threat model. Relevant areas are T-041 (prefix cache) and T-056 (overclaim).

Open integration question: the doc describes a behavior change (default thinking disabled for JSON on Qwen) that implies a code change to the prompt render path in Qwen35TemplateFix and the coordinator prompt sidecar. That code is not in this batch, so I cannot verify it. If the prompt render and the cache-planning render diverge, prefix-cache scoping (cacheSalt, prompt-contract ID, T-041) could be affected. That concerns the correctness of an unseen implementation, not a documented regression, so I record it as uncertainty only. Other batches should check that the prompt-contract ID/cacheSalt derivation still binds to the changed rendering.
